newsitem.title: INDIA: India state seeks Israel's help in militant fight.
newsitem.headline: India state seeks Israel's help in militant fight.

text.p: An Indian state sent a high-level delegation to Israel on Thursday to explore purchasing weapons, helicopters and pilotless aircraft for a fight against Maoist insurgents, police said.

The four-member team led by the home (interior) minister of Andhra Pradesh state, A. Madhava Reddy, is interested in the state-of-the-art equipment to combat left-wing Naxalite guerrillas, state police chief H.J. Dora said.
The Naxalite movement was started in India in the 1960s by groups which split from the main communist party.
Police said Naxalites, who reject the Indian government and want to set up Maoist state of their own, killed 202 civilians and 45 policemen in 1996.
The People's War Group, considered the most violent of the Naxalite groups, controls large forest tracts straddling the states of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa.
Dora said the state delegation, which left on Thursday and was due to return on February 14, was interested in buying a $6 million pilotless reconnaissance aircraft used by Israeli intelligence.
The aircraft can take high resolution photographs of militants and their weapons, he said.
The team will also explore the possibility of buying firearms, advanced police communication equipment and light combat helicopters, Dora said.
Andhra Pradesh authorities stepped up their battle against Naxalites after militants killed 36 policemen in three audacious raids between October and January.
The state government has asked the federal government for some 5,000 paramilitary troops and $10 million for weapons and modernisation of its intelligence gathering network.
